newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber closes up, but buying still thin.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber closes up, but buying still thin.

text.p: Rubber futures finished slightly higher on Monday in a lifeless market with players ignoring the strong prices in Japan which had been inspired by the expiry of the spot November contract there, dealers said.
"There was some shortcovering for RSS3 and TSR20 rubber on nearby months by buyers trying to cover their positions. But volume in other months was very thin," a local rubber trader said.
Some 1,180 tonnes of the local January RSS3 contract and 860 tonnes of the February RSS3 contract was traded. About 1,220 tonnes of the January TSR20 contract was traded.
"The impact of Japan's spot expiry here was limited. Overseas buyers remained asleep," another dealer said.
At around 0945 GMT, January RSS3 was seen at 126.50-126.75 U.S. cents a kg from Friday's settlement of 126.25 cents.
January RSS1 was seen at 182.00-183.00 Singapore cents (US$1.30-$1.31) a kg from the previous 182.25 cents.
January TSR20 was seen at 176.50 Singapore cents (US$1.26) a kg from 176.25 cents.
